A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RocketKV and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. The retained experiments and method components can be matched reliably despite substantial revision and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original LongBench, Needle-in-a-Haystack, and RULER evaluations, H100 efficiency measurements, and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and efficiency results, including new SCBench multi-turn evaluations, A100 measurements, token-selection analysis, and compression-split ablations.

M1.justification: V2 replaces equal square-root compression splitting with an adaptive split factor and replaces sequence-dependent 63/511 pooling with fixed pooling size 63. It also introduces RocketKV-MT, which preserves the full KV history and selects a new subset each turn. Hybrid attention is renamed HSA with its underlying selection steps retained.

E1.justification: LongBench, NIAH, and RULER coverage is retained. V2 adds SCBench multi-turn evaluation on Llama3.1-8B-Ins, testing retrieval, question answering, global operations, and mixed tasks across successive queries. Reusing context across turns introduces a substantial new evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: The separately evaluated SnapKV-GQA variant in v1 Figures 6 and 9 disappears from v2's comparisons. Otherwise, corresponding benchmark tables preserve Full-KV, Exact-TopK, DuoAttention, SnapKV, Quest, SparQ, and standalone Hybrid, renamed HSA. SCBench extends this existing roster.

E3.justification: V2 introduces SCBench budgets of 1024–16384, a 128-token observation window, and a 127,500-token prompt limit; efficiency testing adds A100 alongside H100. The new qasper analysis examines 200 questions using layer 31, head 0. Appendix A.3 also removes v1's explicit generated-token deduction from SnapKV's budget description, leaving that accounting less explicit.

E4.justification: V2 adds a CDF analysis of unique Exact-TopK token selections and compares adaptive compression splitting against fixed factors 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7. V1's GQA-enhancement and pooling-kernel sensitivity studies are removed. Standalone Hybrid/HSA comparisons remain supported by the appendix tables, despite fewer plotted models.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or performance uncertainty estimates. V2's new CDF characterizes token-selection behavior across questions rather than introducing uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: RocketKV and SnapKV values change throughout the retained appendix tables. For example, RocketKV's Llama3.1 RULER-96K average at budget 256 changes from 57.5 to 73.2 under revised method settings (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 9). V2 adds SCBench results and reports maxima of 3.3× on H100, 3.7× on A100, and 32.6% memory savings, versus v1's 3× on H100 and 31.4%.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.6 generalizes the storage derivation from 1/sqrt(c) + 2/c^(3/4) to 1/c^r + 2/c^((1+r)/2), and derives the corresponding RocketKV-MT expression. This extends the existing analytical cost model without introducing a new theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws SnapKV++ as a separately proposed contribution and instead emphasizes adopting SnapKV, adaptive compression decomposition, and RocketKV-MT. The abstract and introduction add multi-turn applicability and near-oracle accuracy claims, plus a 400× compression claim and revised efficiency claims on A100.

C2.justification: V2 explains why permanent eviction fails across turns and explicitly states that RocketKV-MT sacrifices storage savings to preserve context. It adds reasoning for adaptive compression allocation, discusses disaggregated serving, and interprets A100/H100 speedup differences through their memory-bandwidth-to-compute ratios.

D1.justification: V2 documents integer page-size rounding, a worked 64× compression allocation, revised pooling parameters, and SCBench observation-window settings. A100 hardware information is added, while the Python/gpt-fast implementation, FP16 precision, batch size one, and existing benchmark preprocessing remain documented.

R1.justification: V1 claims GQA-compatible SnapKV++ as a contribution; v2 explicitly adopts SnapKV and credits Ada-KV for groupwise selection, materially revising the novelty attribution. Research positioning also expands to SCBench, MLA/DeepSeek, XAttention, and disaggregated serving systems.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and method exposition are substantially rewritten. Existing baseline motivation moves into the introduction, cost analysis is reorganized into adaptive compression and system implications, and the main-text ablation section is restructured within Appendix B.1. Acknowledgment and impact sections are added.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout and rearranges the HSA diagram and pseudocode side by side. It removes the first-stage pseudocode, adds CDF, SCBench, and split-factor displays, expands the efficiency figure to three panels, redraws heatmaps, and reorganizes appendix tables.

improvement.justification: V2 exposes a multi-turn failure untested in v1 and evaluates a targeted remedy: at budget 1024, Table 4 reports 44.3 for RocketKV-MT, 26.6 for RocketKV, and 45.0 for Exact-TopK. Explicit storage tradeoffs, compression-split ablations, and clearer attribution substantially strengthen applicability and scientific support. These gains outweigh the removed GQA/kernel ablations, although SnapKV budget accounting becomes less explicit and the headline speedup includes newly tested hardware.
